text:
amy: customer reports repeated SSE disconnects + partial event delivery. They see clients reconnecting ~2-3x per minute and billing spike for token/connection churn. trace_id=trc_9f3b
raj: quick grep on their dedicated pool shows repeated socket write errors on host redpool-7: `writev(...) -> -1, errno=EAGAIN` then later `sendmsg -> -1, errno=EPIPE`. Connection state shows large per-conn queue growth before abort.
elle: which client stack and where are they sitting? browser? proxy?
amy: Browser EventSource behind an express proxy (our infra). Client slow-consumer (JS handler sleeps ~700ms). Repro attached below (minimal node fetch + slow handler).
amy: repro steps:
```
# reproduce locally (node)
# start simple SSE server that emits small JSON every 100ms
node sse-server.js &
# client that reads slowly (~700ms per event)
node slow-client.js
```
raj: logs from redpool-7 around the incident: 
```
[2024-06-25T14:11:22Z] conn=98765 sendq=62432 sndbuf=87380 writev=-1 errno=EAGAIN
[2024-06-25T14:11:22Z] conn=98765 queued_bytes=512000 high_water=524288 
[2024-06-25T14:11:23Z] conn=98765 send() -> -1 errno=EPIPE (client closed)
[2024-06-25T14:11:23Z] stream aborted -> partial chunk flushed
```
amy: note: proxy returns 499 (client closed) in front, upstream sees partial frames and aborts; downstream billing counts tokens for produced partials then reconnects.
ops-oncall: we've already bumped SO_SNDBUF on a few hosts and enabled keepalive tweaks, but this just masks the slow-consumer pattern. Root cause seems client-side slowness + our bursty emit rate.
eng-runtime: can you confirm how the runtime handles EAGAIN and whether we abort stream vs. backpressure-wait? Is there a per-connection queue cap?
eng-runtime: current behavior: we allow per-connection in-memory queue up to 512KB, then if socket is nonblocking and write returns EAGAIN we track and if queue > high_water we abort with a soft-close to avoid head-of-line. We do not currently implement durable on-disk spill for streams.
elle: customer asked for mitigation ASAP. Can we: 1) reduce default per-request chunk size (e.g., 32KB -> 8KB), 2) add early 429 when queue crosses threshold, 3) make partial chunk semantics clearer (so client can resume without double-billing)?
raj: short-term: reduce emit rate (throttle generator) and set smaller chunks in proxy. Medium: enforce per-client concurrency and return 429 when queue>256KB. Long: consider streaming spill-to-disk or backpressure signals to generator (pause production).
amy: I attached the minimal repro code snippet and a trace dump. Key lines: `queued_bytes` climbs to ~500KB then we get EAGAIN; after ~1s client closes -> EPIPE. Billing spike corresponds to number of token-producing writes before closure.
support-bot: escalated to #eng-runtime and #eng-sre with trace trc_9f3b.
ops-oncall: I'll apply a temporary throttling rule to the customer's route (rate-limit bursts) and roll a config change to set max per-conn queue to 256KB. Will monitor metrics (stream.write_failures, conn_queue_bytes).
eng-runtime: will follow up with a patch to: 1) emit server-side backpressure metrics, 2) lower default chunking for SSE endpoints, 3) return clear streaming error codes so clients can differentiate aborted vs soft-close and avoid replay/billing double-counts.
amy: thanks. Customer asked for repro steps so they can test client-side fix (process events faster or increase their keepalive). Sent contact info.
elle: leave this open for 48h and collect any new traces. If we see the same pattern after throttling, we'll schedule an incident postmortem. :thumbsup:
